Include keywords in URLs, metadata and content.
Use relevant keywords as the anchor text (for example, don’t use ‘click here’ as link text).

rules.specification: The page does not specify target keywords, minimum frequency, or whether every individual heading, link or image description must contain keywords. These details require editorial interpretation; do not invent a keyword-density threshold.
rules.violation_condition: Relevant keywords are missing from the specified textual components of a webpage.
when: Applies to URLs, metadata, headings, page content, link text, and image captions and alt text.
Does not require adding otherwise unnecessary links, images or captions.
rules.why: G-2 groups the locations of the same keyword-inclusion check; G-4 absorbs repeated keyword instructions.

rules.quote: Create URLs that contain words from the title of the page
rules.violation_condition: A page URL contains no words from that page’s title.
when: Compare the URL wording with the title of the page it identifies.
rules.why: The title-word relationship is a distinct check from keyword inclusion and keyword position.

rules.quote: Create URLs that contain words from the title of the page with the main keywords close to the start.
rules.specification: This item concerns keyword position only. The manual does not define ‘close to the start’ or explain whether position is measured from the hostname or the page-specific path.
rules.violation_condition: The main keywords occur late in a page URL rather than close to its start.
when: Assess the position of the page’s main keywords within its URL.
rules.why: Keyword position can be wrong even when the URL contains both keywords and title words, so it is a separate finding.

rules.quote: The URL should be below 100 characters
rules.violation_condition: A page URL contains 100 or more characters.
when: Applies to the page URL.
rules.why: URL length and intelligibility are independently checkable properties, so they are separated.

rules.specification: The manual supplies no test for whether a URL makes sense to its intended users. Assessment needs the page context and audience.
rules.violation_condition: A page URL is unintelligible to its intended users.
when: Assess the URL in the context of its page and intended users.
rules.why: Intelligibility is a textual property of the URL and is independent of its character count.

examples.note: The example also illustrates a readable, title-derived URL, but it is attached to the nearest separator rule (E-2).

rules.quote: To separate words in the URL, use hyphens instead of spaces or underscores.
rules.violation_condition: Spaces or underscores, rather than hyphens, separate words in a page URL.
when: Applies where a separator is used between words in a URL, not to punctuation serving another URL function.
rules.why: This is one separator-choice check; spaces and underscores are alternative violations of it.

rules.violation_condition: The same page title is reused on different pages of a website.
when: Requires comparison with titles of other pages on the website.
rules.why: Title uniqueness is independent of title length, clarity and keyword inclusion.

rules.violation_condition: A page title contains more than 70 characters.
when: Applies to the page title used in metadata and search results.
rules.why: The explicit title-length limit produces a finding separate from the other title requirements.

covers.quote: This is the first thing a screen reader user will hear and needs to assure them they are on the right page.

rules.violation_condition: A page title does not clearly identify the page’s subject, leaving users unable to tell whether they are on the right page.
when: Assess the title against the page’s content and intended users.
rules.why: G-1 uses the specific title instruction rather than making the metadata section’s general introduction another rule.

covers.quote: This helps users to know if it’s what they need.

rules.quote: Describe the content in plain language.
rules.violation_condition: A meta description does not explain the page’s content in language that its intended users can readily understand and use to judge its relevance.
when: Applies to the meta description, not a search-engine-generated content snippet.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the user-focused explanation with the specific plain-language description instruction; keyword inclusion remains a separate check.

rules.quote: They can be up to 160 characters.
rules.violation_condition: A meta description contains more than 160 characters.
when: Applies to the meta description field, not a search-engine-generated content snippet.
rules.why: This establishes a checkable upper bound rather than a free-standing permission under G-3.

rules.quote: Link to content on other quality sites
rules.specification: The manual does not define site quality. Assessment requires information about the destination, not merely the visible URL.
rules.violation_condition: An external link points to content on a low-quality site.
when: Applies when linking to content on other websites.
rules.why: Destination quality and link placement are independent properties and therefore separate checks.

rules.quote: Link to content on other quality sites towards the end of the content.
rules.specification: This item concerns placement only. The manual gives no paragraph, section or proportional boundary for ‘towards the end’.
rules.violation_condition: Links to content on other websites are positioned away from the end of the page’s content.
when: Applies to links to other websites, not internal links.
rules.why: Link placement can be wrong even when the destination is high quality, so it warrants its own finding.

covers.quote: Ensure the linking text to this page relates to the title.

examples.note: The explanatory block identifies which words are linked; it is not part of the example sentence.

parts.quote: Make sure users can read content on all devices using responsive design methods.
[The text ‘responsive design methods’ links to a page about consistent and responsive design.]

rules.quote: Write link text that makes the destination and purpose of the link clear.
rules.violation_condition: Link text fails to make its destination and purpose clear, including wording unrelated to the destination page’s title.
when: Applies to internal and external links.
For a link to a page, consider the destination page’s title when assessing the wording.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates title-related link wording with the destination-clarity check instead of creating overlapping findings.
